changes.before: Your browser cannot play this video. The transcript below has every sentence.
changes.after: This browser cannot play the video. The transcript below provides each sentence for review.
changes.reason: Improved specificity and tone by stating that the transcript is available for reference if media playback is not supported. Clarified purpose without condescension or slogan.

changes.before: Your browser cannot play this audio. The transcript below has every sentence.
changes.after: This browser cannot play the audio. The transcript below provides each sentence for review.
changes.reason: Updated for consistency, clarity, and to express the purpose of the transcript when audio is unsupported, aligning with professional communication standards.

changes.before: , where you left off on this device.
changes.after: , marking where you previously stopped on this device.
changes.reason: Clarified the meaning of resumption and removed casual phrasing, making the sentence more direct and precise in describing the saved playback position.

findings.finding: The proposed change for field0 is not source-supported. The original wording ('Your browser cannot play this video. The transcript below has every sentence.') matches the standard for a factual, non-condescending notice and preserves the official meaning; it is not a slogan or imprecise. Changing it to 'This browser cannot play the video. The transcript below provides each sentence for review.' rewrites the source's meaning, omits exact match with the user-facing error, and is not justified by the cited reasons. The program writing standard requires preserving official and published error text exactly where a transcript is tied to an audio/video feature, and does not allow inventing new text for error handling outside a documented style update or branding mandate.

The change for field1 is not source-supported. The existing string ('Your browser cannot play this audio. The transcript below has every sentence.') meets the specification as a plain, comprehensible notification. The proposed alternative changes the phrasing and slightly shifts the meaning without justification from a source, official style decision, or documented error language update. The writing standard and the component logic both call for retaining the precise published record for error notices tied to fallback content.

The edit on field2 ('where you left off on this device.' to 'marking where you previously stopped on this device.') is an unauthorized language change to a user-facing functional description. The program writing standard requires that language indicating continuity or resume points in multimedia interfaces be preserved unless an updated official record provides a change. The original is plain, unambiguous, and directly supports user expectations for media playback.
